question: Why do we say "trick or treat"?
notes: Narration v3. Times are seconds into voice.mp3, computed from words.json by shots.py. Each scene is one stop on the vertical paper strip. "paint" lists where the paint lands and the word it lands on.

scenes.line: Why do we say "trick or treat"?

art.desc: A jack-o'-lantern bucket full of wrapped candy (Short 09's last picture)

scenes.beat_note: Opens on Short 09's last picture (the thread).

scenes.line: Because it started as a threat. A hundred years ago, Halloween meant pranks: gates carried off, wagons hauled onto roofs.

art.desc: A farm wagon hauled up onto a barn roof: a Halloween prank

scenes.line: In 1917, an Ontario newspaper printed the earliest known use of "tricks or treats." Gangs of kids called it out at the door.

art.desc: Four kids in paper masks at a front door, seen from behind

scenes.line: Pay them off, the paper said, and your house was safe.

art.desc: A hand from a doorway dropping a coin into a child's palm
A plain two-storey house, front door shut (Short 02)

scenes.line: By the 1970s, the fear flipped. Now the danger was the treat. Parents were warned that strangers hid poison and razor blades in it.

art.desc: An apple cut in half on a plate, a razor blade beside it
A corked glass bottle (Short 02): the poison

scenes.line: But a sociologist has tracked these reports all the way back to 1958. He hasn't found one child killed or badly hurt by a stranger's candy.

art.desc: A file box of newspaper clippings with a magnifying glass

scenes.line: The most famous death, in 1974, was a boy poisoned by his own father.
Still, homemade treats got thrown out.

art.desc: A trash can full of homemade cookies and popcorn balls

scenes.line: Only candy in a factory wrapper counted as safe.

art.desc: One candy bar in a sealed factory wrapper

scenes.line: Kids once got treats to stop a real threat. Now the treats come sealed, against a stranger who, as far as anyone knows, never killed a child.

art.desc: A hand from a doorway dropping a coin into a child's palm
One candy bar in a sealed factory wrapper

scenes.line: And why did New York kids once go door to door in costume on Thanksgiving? That's another story.

art.desc: A kid in baggy grown-up clothes and a mask holding out a hat at a door with a paper turkey

scenes.beat_note: The tease: Short 11 is Ragamuffin Day.
